newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - April 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - April 10.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Simmering conflicts in the coalition government over truck freight limits have flared up when Interior Minister Sanoh Thienthong threatened to resign after the prime minister showed support for maintaining the 21-tonne limit. Sanoh made the threat before the Joint Public-Private Sector Consultative Committee after Chavalit Yongchaiyudh, the prime minister, who chaired the meeting, opposed a change. (THE NATION) (BANGKOK POST)

- Deputy Prime Minister Samak Sundaravej has threatened to sue a leader of the Forum of the Poor for defamation. The Prachakorn Thai Party leader was accused by Wanida Tantiwittayapitak of assaulting a protesting farmer who helped block an entrances to Government House on Tuesday. Samak, who was unable to get to a doctor's appointment, engaged in a lively debate with the protesters. (BANGKOK POST)

- The Thailand Development Research Institute opposes the direct election of prime ministers and the separation of the power of the executive and legislative branches of government, arguing it could have a negative effect on the political system. Public opinion strongly favours the direct election of the prime minister according to opinion surveys by members of the Constitution Drafting Assembly and major pollsters. (THE NATION) (BANGKOK POST)

- Right in the middle of the Thai government's road show to offer US$500 to 700 million in Yankee bonds, Moody's Investors Service, the U.S. credit rating agency, announced a downgrade of foreign currency ceilings for bonds and bank deposits of Thailand from A2 to A3. A final pricing of the bonds is expected to be concluded today, following a five-day road show that is taking a Thai delegation headed by Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan to Boston, Chicago and New York. (THE NATION, BANGKOK POST)

- The export-import situation has shown signs of improvement during the first two months of the year, says Commerce Minister Narongchai Akrasanee. Speaking after discussions with senior officials on the business economy situation during the first quarter of 1997, Narongchai says information in hand indicates that the country's exports are stabilising and showing signs of recovery. (BUSINESS DAY)

- Shinawatra Group has won a significant victory with the Telephone Organisation of Thailand which will set it become a fully-fledged multimedia network provider in direct competition with TelecomAsia Plc. The new business is expected to secure the long-term growth of Shinawatra as the sophisticated network could serve the growing demand for large-volume high-speed data transmission facilities for such things as the Internet and other new information technology services. (THE NATION).
